Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic rapidly affected the globe, causing particularly devastating impacts in China, where online misinformation and false rumors surged due to the pandemic's high visibility. Central to the research is a quantification model developed to capture the "false news index," designed to efficiently track the pandemic's intensity, the prevalence of false information, and underlying user behavior. a strong geodetic set is a vertex subset \(S\subseteq V(G)\) capable of covering all vertices in \(V(G) \setminus S\) via unique shortest paths between every distinct pair of elements within \(S\). The Strong Geodetic (SG) decision problem takes a graph \(G\) and an integer \(k\) as input, asking whether a strong geodetic set of size at most \(k\) exists. This problem is established as NP-hard for general graphs. This work extends the SG problem by introducing the Strong Geodetic (SG) decision problem on the class of chordal graphs to analyze its computational tractability. To determine the complexity, we investigate several related issues, beginning with an examination of the problem on trees, where demonstrably a solution of size at most \(k\) can be verified efficiently in polynomial time, thus proving the problem to be in that class for tree structures as a means to establish complexity on the broader class of chordal graphs.
